rationale: Baseline race: single job claimed then cancelled while handler runs normally; completion update races cancellation update on same row, exposing lost-update or wrong terminal state.
Two sessions poll empty then race to claim one job while cancellation runs after first claim; exposes claim serialization failure, double-claim, or cancel applied to wrong owner.
One worker claims first job then both jobs are cancelled, covering claimed versus still-queued cancel paths and dequeue-versus-cancel race for second job; exposes resurrection or missed cancel.
Two workers concurrently claim two jobs with retries allowed while both are cancelled after first claim; exposes attempt-count versus cancel-flag race and whether cancel suppresses retry.
Single worker processes three jobs with partial cancel and retries allowed; cancels span claimed and queued jobs while one job remains uncancelled as control, exposing scoping errors and state bleed.

Maximum contention: two workers claim and complete three jobs with retries allowed while all three are cancelled; stresses cross-session claim, retry, and cancel interleavings for duplicate execution or inconsistent states.
